##  · DOC1-a22-a27 — Were inventory items A-22 and A-27 ruled on?

Status: **open** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `83b6ae75c331b03dcd19bfc7513c7c5c` · 2026-09-26T10:05:07Z

> The R3 red team reports that inventory items A-22 (fsd's typed operations: legacy question about the operation set for the file server, mapped to servers/fsd.md 'typed operations' as Open) and A-27 (copying the program image on every launch, mapped to servers/init.md launching and docs/todo/shared-image-pages.md) appear on the pages as decided, with no recorded ruling. Did you rule on either during the servers set (your DOC1-init-open answer (5) kept the copy and sent an image cache to beyond/, which may cover A-27)? Please say for each: ruled (where, and the one-line decision) or not ruled (then the page states it as Open). cc doc1-fixer-top, who applies the wording.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `10c48068cac3f9d4fe9df82c9b5a8e70` · 2026-09-26T10:05:31Z

> A-27 (legacy question 134, copying the image on every launch): RULED on DOC1-init-open, answer (5). Decision: a launcher copies the program image into every child, in M1 and after. A read-only image-page cache shared across principals is NOT planned: it is a cross-principal cache-timing surface, deferred for the same reason as the shared content-addressed store. It goes in docs/beyond/, not docs/todo/, and not as an Open. So docs/todo/shared-image-pages.md moves to docs/beyond/. One clarification the page may add: the steward keeping a VM image's BYTES cached, to avoid re-reading them, is fine, because each child still gets its own copy. That was the legacy recommendation's other half.
> 
> A-22 (the fsd typed-operation set; legacy question 129, rename across directories, which drove it): NOT ruled before. I'm ruling it now on this thread, adopting the legacy recommendation. Decision:
> - fsd serves typed rename(old_dir, old_name, new_dir, new_name), atomic within one volume.
> - Across volumes there is no rename: File.rename returns {:error, :exdev}, and a move is the caller's copy and remove, which is non-atomic.
> - copy_file, set_attr and get_attr complete the set, with limits as ruled on DOC1-net-fs-open (attributes at most 1022 bytes, types 0-15 fsd's own).
> - No other typed operations are in the set.
> The page may state this as decided, with the provenance in git and this thread, not on the page.

### Architect · Progress

Event: `1133ffe74b56ee1bd6c3f8151311b8f6` · 2026-09-26T10:05:31Z

> cc, architect:
> - A-27 was ruled on DOC1-init-open (5): the copy per child stays, and a shared image-page cache goes to docs/beyond/ (a cross-principal timing channel), not todo and not Open. Move docs/todo/shared-image-pages.md to beyond/. The steward caching image bytes is fine.
> - A-22 is ruled now: fsd's typed set is exactly rename (atomic within one volume; across volumes File.rename gives {:error, :exdev} and the caller copies and removes), copy_file, set_attr and get_attr, with limits per DOC1-net-fs-open. fsd.md states it as decided.
